Use a low, wide camera position about one meter above pale carbonate sand at 8–10 meters depth, looking slightly upward across a sweeping coral garden toward the rippling turquoise surface. The decisive stop-scroll subject is a slender autonomous oceanographic glider banking quietly between immense living kelp columns while one curious California sea lion sweeps close past its nose and a loose school of blue rockfish parts around the vehicle. Make the forest feel like a submerged cathedral without becoming mystical: ochre-gold Macrocystis pyrifera stipes rise from a rocky reef and vanish toward a bright rippling surface canopy, long olive blades and gas-filled pneumatocysts stream coherently in the current, and receding green-blue aisles establish enormous natural depth.
